chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Abu al-Maghra, from al-Halbi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Every interest (riba) that people consumed due to ignorance, then repented, it is accepted from them if their repentance is recognized from them.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man inherited wealth from his father and knew that there was interest in that wealth, but it had been mixed in trade with other permissible wealth, then the permissible part is permissible and good, so let him consume it; and if he recognizes something from it that is interest, let him take the capital of his wealth and return the interest.'

And whoever man acquired much wealth in which he had increased with interest, and was ignorant of that, then recognized it afterwards, and intended to remove it from what has passed, it is for him, and he should leave it regarding what he resumes.
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim handle inherited wealth that is mixed with interest (riba)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that ignorance of riba in mixed wealth excuses the owner, allowing them to retain the principal and purify the remainder by extracting the interest, whereas those who knowingly accumulate riba must return the excess. This ruling reflects the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and practical ease (*taysir*) in financial transactions, distinguishing between accidental mixing and deliberate accumulation. The hadith emphasizes that repentance and identification of the interest are key to validating the remaining wealth.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abu Al Magra, from Al Halby who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every interest which the people consume due to ignorance, then repent, so it would be Accepted from them, then the repentance is recognised from them’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a man were to inherit some wealth from his father and has recognised that interest is among that wealth, but it has been mixed up in the business with other than Permissible that which was Permissible and good, so let him eat it; and if he recognises anything from it that is interest, so let him take the capital of his wealth and let him return the interest.

And whichever man benefits with a lot of wealth and most of it is from the interest, so he was ignorant of that, then he recognises it afterwards, so he intends that he removes it from it regarding what is past, so it is for him, and he should leave with regards to what he resumes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from al-Washsha’ from abu al-Mighra’ from al-Halabiy, who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Any kind of Riba ’ people have consumed in ignorance then repented, such repentance is accepted if such repentance is found in them.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘If a man inherits goods, from his father and knows that there is Riba ’ in it but is mixed in trade with other lawful goods it is lawful and clean for him and he has permission to consume such properties. If however, he comes to know the Riba ’ item, he then must separate his capital and return the Riba’ property.

If one earns a great deal of property in which there is a great deal of Riba’ but does not know such property exactly and afterwards comes to know it and wants to remove it, what is passed is for him but he must stay away from Riba ’ in coming times.’”
